reason: S1 makes scan completion and pixel swizzling depend on state observed at decoder suspension boundaries: decoder.decode_sos increments scan_count, while decoder.decode_frame compares that state after decoder.do_decode_frame returns and before yield? ddf_status. H0 supplies one existing io_buffer and exits whenever decode_frame returns a non-OK status, so it cannot refill the source and resume the same decoder after a short-read suspension. Although incremental decoding existed in S0, S0 swizzled directly at the end of decode_sos; S1 newly defers and coalesces that work according to scan_count across outer coroutine returns. This materially aggravates the historical streaming-protocol gap because chunk boundaries can now control the changed behavior.
evidence: S1 adds decoder.scan_count and increments it with `this.scan_count ~sat+= 1` after a scan completes in decoder.decode_sos.
S1 decoder.decode_frame snapshots `scan_count = this.scan_count`, calls `this.do_decode_frame?`, and swizzles only when `scan_count < this.scan_count`.
S1 decoder.decode_frame then propagates suspensions through `yield? ddf_status`, making the new decision occur at the public API's yield boundary.

H0's fuzz_image_decoder calls wuffs_base__image_decoder__decode_frame once for each frame-config iteration and immediately goes to exit for every non-OK status; it contains no source refill or same-frame short-read resumption path.
S0 performed swizzle_gray or swizzle_colorful directly at the end of decoder.decode_sos, without scan_count or outer-yield-dependent coalescing.
recommended_action: Add a hash-controlled incremental-input mode that exposes the JPEG bytes in multiple chunks, resumes decode_frame on short-read with the same decoder and pixel buffer, and varies chunk boundaries around completed scans, especially for progressive grayscale and colorful JPEGs.
